card.title: We Always Did This
card.instruction: Treat the strangest behavior in the scene as an old shared tradition that needs no explanation and deserves immediate continuation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Walk backwards to dessert, like every family Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say that before the backward part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spill my tea. Can you carry it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. That's why we link elbows. Gran always said nobody should reach pudding alone.

mechanism: A treats backward walking to dessert as an unquestionable family custom and incorporates B's practical tea concern into its supposed established method.
confusable: Unlike inventing a new ritual to manage feelings, A claims the bizarre act already belongs to shared history and must continue.
comparison: The backward-walk alternative converts help with tea into a linked-elbow tradition; the ancestor alternative adapts seating through a claimed pudding-bearer custom.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
